source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
2. Gather relevant data: Ensure you collect comprehensive data on various pollutants such as sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and any other specific pollutants regulated in your locality.

3. Use accurate monitoring instruments: Utilize calibrated and high-quality air quality monitoring equipment to ensure precise measurements. Regularly maintain and calibrate the equipment as per manufacturer recommendations.

4. Capture weather data: Align your emissions data with meteorological data such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and direction. Weather conditions significantly influence the dispersion and concentration of pollutants.

5. Document the location and time: Record the precise location of emission monitoring points, including geographic coordinates, and the exact time of each reading. This is crucial to track emission trends and identify the sources leading to excessive pollution.

6. Record baseline data: Measure and document ambient
